title: Spring Boot REST Controllers: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision notes for building Spring MVC REST endpoints: controller mapping, input binding, bodies and validation, ResponseEntity, centralized exception handling and content negotiation.

chapters.title: REST Controller Mental Model
points: @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody: every return value is written to the response body via HttpMessageConverters, never resolved as a view name
Request flow: DispatcherServlet → HandlerMapping finds the @RequestMapping method → HandlerAdapter binds arguments → method runs → return value converted by HttpMessageConverter
Controller stays thin: parse and validate input, delegate to a service, return DTOs (not JPA entities) so the API shape is decoupled from the DB schema
Class-level @RequestMapping("/api/users") sets a prefix; method-level @GetMapping/@PostMapping/@PutMapping/@PatchMapping/@DeleteMapping are shortcuts for @RequestMapping(method=...)
Controllers are singleton beans: never keep per-request state in fields

chapters.title: Request Mapping, Path Variables and Query Params
points: @GetMapping("/{id}") with @PathVariable Long id binds the URI segment; name must match the placeholder or use @PathVariable("id")
@RequestParam String q reads ?q=...; it is required by default, so a missing param gives 400. Use required=false or defaultValue="10" to relax
Narrow a mapping with consumes = "application/json" and produces = "application/json"; mismatches return 415 and 406
Optional<T> or a wrapper type with @RequestParam/@PathVariable makes it optional; a primitive with a missing value fails with 400 or 500
Example: @GetMapping("/users/{id}/orders") public List<OrderDto> list(@PathVariable Long id, @RequestParam(defaultValue="0") int page, @RequestHeader("X-Trace") String t)

chapters.title: Request Bodies and Bean Validation
points: @RequestBody deserializes the JSON body into a DTO via Jackson; malformed JSON throws HttpMessageNotReadableException → 400
Add @Valid (or @Validated) before @RequestBody to trigger Bean Validation; failure throws MethodArgumentNotValidException → 400
Constraints go on DTO fields: @NotNull (not null), @NotEmpty (not null or empty), @NotBlank (non-blank string), @Size, @Min/@Max, @Email, @Pattern
Validating @PathVariable/@RequestParam needs @Validated on the class plus constraints on the params; failure throws ConstraintViolationException (a different exception from body validation)
Example: record CreateUser(@NotBlank String name, @Email String email, @Min(18) int age) {} then create(@Valid @RequestBody CreateUser req)

chapters.title: ResponseEntity and Status Codes
points: ResponseEntity<T> controls status, headers and body together; returning a plain object defaults to 200
Builders: ResponseEntity.ok(body), ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.CREATED).body(x), ResponseEntity.noContent().build(), ResponseEntity.notFound().build()
Create returns 201 plus Location header: ResponseEntity.created(URI.create("/api/users/" + id)).body(dto)
@ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED) on a method sets a fixed status; use ResponseEntity when status varies at runtime
Status conventions: GET 200, POST 201, PUT/PATCH 200, DELETE 204, bad input 400, missing 404, conflict 409, validation 422 or 400

chapters.title: Exception Handling and Content Negotiation
points: @RestControllerAdvice (= @ControllerAdvice + @ResponseBody) holds global handlers; @ControllerAdvice alone needs @ResponseBody on each handler
@ExceptionHandler(UserNotFoundException.class) returns ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> with 404; the most specific exception type wins
Handle MethodArgumentNotValidException with ex.getBindingResult().getFieldErrors() and return a field → message map
Use @ResponseStatus(NOT_FOUND) on a custom exception class for a simple mapping; ProblemDetail (RFC 7807) is the built-in standard error body in Spring 6+
Content negotiation picks the converter from the Accept header and the produces attribute; JSON via Jackson is the default, XML needs jackson-dataformat-xml on the classpath; no match returns 406

chapters.title: Spring REST Cheat Sheet
points: Annotations: @RestController, @RequestMapping, @GetMapping/@PostMapping, @PathVariable, @RequestParam, @RequestBody, @Valid, @RequestHeader
Error codes: malformed JSON 400, @Valid failure 400, wrong Content-Type 415, no acceptable Accept 406, unknown route 404, wrong verb 405
Exceptions: MethodArgumentNotValidException (body), ConstraintViolationException (params), HttpMessageNotReadableException (bad JSON)
Common mistakes: returning entities, forgetting @Valid, missing @Validated for param constraints, swallowing exceptions into 200, using @Controller without @ResponseBody
Pattern: thin controller → service → DTO response → one @RestControllerAdvice for all errors
